key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Progressive over months to years, acute decompensation possible. LOCATION: Chest (retrosternal angina), generalized dyspnea. DURATION: Progressive symptoms. CHARACTER: Exertional angina (pressure, squeezing), exertional dyspnea, exertional syncope (classic triad: angina, dyspnea, syncope). AGGRAVATING: EXERTION (angina and syncope), lying flat (dyspnea). RELIEVING: Rest. TIMING: Predictable with exertion. SEVERITY: Variable, 5-8/10 for angina. KEY POSITIVES: Elderly patient, harsh systolic ejection murmur (loudest at right upper sternal border), radiates to carotids, narrow pulse pressure, delayed carotid upstroke, history of bicuspid aortic valve. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT at rest typically.
